methods: Statistical simulation of microbial DNA data decay
claims: Repetition reduces the risk of block loss but increases the total number of inserted bases and lowers nominal payload density.
Increasing genomic redundancy to two copies with ten reads per copy achieves a mean recovery accuracy of 0.990 over extended generations.
Selection favoring mutated variants drastically accelerates payload loss relative to neutral evolutionary benchmarks.
summary: This study uses statistical simulations to evaluate the long-term reliability and physical payload cost of storing digital data within living microbial genomes subject to evolutionary mutation and selection.
